title: Taranga 14. Srimad Acharya's Travels to the Homes of His Disciples, and Other Events
html:
Jiva Gosvami's four letters to Srinivasa; Ramachandra Kaviraja at Yajigrama; Srinivasa at Budhari and Borakuli: the installation of Sri Radha-vinoda, the festival and sankirtana; the journey to Kheturi, farewell to Narottama; talk of the Acharya's virtues and of false teachers; Virachandra's letter; songs about Srinivasa

1Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the refuge of all!
Glory to Nityananda Rama, the son of Rohini!

2Glory to Sri Advaitachandra, the son of Kuvera!
Glory to Gadadhara, whose life is Gauranga!

3Glory, glory to Srivasa and Murari, full of prema!
Glory, glory to Vakreshvara, the abode of virtues!

4Glory to Haridasa, glory to Gadadhara Dasa!
Glory to Pundarika Vidyanidhi and Shuklambara!

5Glory to Narahari, Gauridasa and Dhananjaya!
Glory to Ramananda, the son of Bhavananda!

6Glory to Sri Vijaya, Vasu, Madhava and Mukunda!
Glory to Kashishvara, Yadu and Sri Paramananda!

7Glory, glory to Sri Nandana and Acharyaratna!1
Glory to Rupa and Sanatana, dear to Gaurachandra!

8Glory to Raghunatha, Raghunatha and Sri Gopala!
[Glory] to Sri Bhugarbha, Lokanatha and the merciful Sri Jiva!

9Glory, glory to the devotees of Sri Gaurachandra,
by remembering whom one obtains the treasure of bhakti!

10Glory, glory to the listeners, the abode of virtues!
Now, with kind hearts, listen to what I tell.

11Sri Acharya Thakura, his mind full of supreme bliss,
always savours the books of bhakti together with his [disciples].

12By the Lord's mercy he is a teacher in all the shastras;
he always crushes the pride of the opponents of bhakti.

13There is no end to the Acharya's prema-bhakti and deeds —
he whom Sri Jiva Gosani honours so highly.

14Who can tell what Sri Jiva's affection is like?
From Vraja he writes merciful letters to the Acharya.

15One day the Acharya says to his [disciples]:
"A letter from Gosani is due to come — why is it delayed?"

16At that very moment the wise Sri Vasanta Raya
came with a letter to the Acharya's assembly.

17Telling the news of Vraja in a few words,
he gave the Acharya Sri Jiva Gosani's letter.

18The Acharya took the letter with great reverence
and reads it, his heart drenched with the tears of his eyes.
The holy letter (1).2
Glory to Sri Vrindavana-natha!
Blessings! To the feet of Sri Srinivasa Acharya, whose two feet bestow all my happiness, — he who is named Jiva, offering obeisances, informs.
I always wish for your well-being; but for many days [news] of it has not come — so do gladden us with it.
I am at present in bodily health, and the others are likewise. But the special [news] is this: the revered Sri Bhugarbha Gosvami has left his body, and his very self he has consciously offered to Sri Vrindavana-natha.
Write of the well-being of your people, especially of Sri Vrindavana Dasa, and also whether he is studying a little or not.
Further, write also how and where Sri Vyasa Sharma or Sri Vasudeva Kaviraja is.
Moreover, the corrections of the Rasamrita-sindhu, the Sri Madhava-mahotsava, the Uttara-champu and the Hari-namamrita are still somewhat unfinished, and besides [it is now] the rainy season, — so they have not been sent now; later, by the favour of providence, they will be sent.3
And further: accept the due obeisances and so on of everyone here; and to those there, [convey] my obeisances and so on.4
The month of Bhadra, the bright fortnight.5
To the honourable king — blessings.

19He whose name in the letter is Vrindavana Dasa
is known as the Acharya's eldest son.6

20As soon as the son was born, the news reached Vraja;
Sri Jiva Gosvami joyfully gave him this name.

21Vyasa and Vasudeva are two disciples of the Acharya;
"the king" is Sri Vira Hambira, the noblest of heart.

22Such is one letter. A few days later a letter again came to the Acharya; in the assembly the Acharya reads the letter. The holy letter (2). Glory to Sri Vrindavana-natha! Blessings! To the greatest Sri Srinivasa Acharya, the best of friends, praised for all virtues, — from here, from Sri Vrindavana, from him who is named Jiva, [a message] with obeisances, embraces and good wishes. Here there is well-being: the desired [happiness] — living in Sri Vrindavana — abides unbroken. Though I am eager to learn of all your [affairs], from time to time my heart is pained by not hearing of them or by hearing the contrary. Therefore I should be consoled by being told of them in a timely and fitting way. Further: the reply to your previous letter we have already written earlier. And now we inform you: grief is opposed to devotion to the Lord and burns the senses and the body; one might indulge in it only if the one mourned would thereby return.7 And further: this Sri Shyamadasa Acharya is devoted to the highest goal, akin to you in spirit, and learned; therefore it is fitting, in close association with him, to discuss devotion to the Lord and so on, — with such a helper the pashandas too will be crushed. Now, having corrected and examined them, these [persons] are bringing there the books Vaishnava-toshani, Durgama-sangamani and Sri Gopala-champu. Therefore keep close company with them for the correction of the books and for discussion, and regard him as your own, to be cared for. Moreover, the Hari-namamrita-vyakarana that was sent to you earlier — if it is being taught, then its errors and so on should be corrected by consulting the bhashya and the like, the vritti and the like. There is also another book here — a supplement; if it is wanted, send word. Now the Srimad Uttara-gopala-champu has been written, but it still has to be examined, — this is made known.8 When will such good fortune come again — association with you? So even from afar one should constantly keep [each other] in remembrance.9 To Sri Vrindavana Dasa and the others — good wishes. To Sri Gopala Dasa and the rest — good wishes. To the feet of Sri Srinivasa Acharya.

23He whose name in the letter is Shyamadasa Acharya
is the son of Vyasa Acharya, now living.10

24Vrindavana Dasa is the son of Srinivasa;
by the words "and the others," know, [are meant] his brothers and sisters.

25Sri Gopala Dasa is the son of Vira Hambira;
this name was given him by Sri Jiva Gosvami.

26The name Sri Dhari Hambira is known everywhere.
Sri Jiva Gosvami wishes all of them well.

27Such is one letter.
Just as the Gosvami's letters come to the Acharya,
so too the Acharya sends letters to the Gosvami.

28News constantly comes with the Vaishnavas who travel back and forth;
the joy [that] the letters [bring] I cannot describe.

29Acharya Thakura enjoys [his life] in Yajigrama;
his heart longs to see Ramachandra.

30Ramachandra, Narottama and Sri Govinda — all three —
in the village of Sri Kheturi are always intoxicated with sankirtana.

31One day, as all three were sitting [together],
at that time Sri Jiva's letter arrived.

32Placing the letter on his head with the greatest reverence, Govinda, overcome with prema, reads the letter. The holy letter (3). Glory to Sri Vrindavana-chandra! Blessings! To those named Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja, Sri Narottama Dasa and Sri Govinda Dasa, praised by all the Vaishnavas, — the treasure in which the happiness of such as me abides, — I, named Jiva, from Sri Vrindavana, with an embrace, make known:11 my particular wish is your well-being. Having received a letter full of affection, I long again and again for the same. In it, out of affection for me, beautiful songs were sent, — by this I am joined with the greatest good. What more [need be said] to those whose affection is without motive? As for the method of constant remembrance that you ask about, — it is clearly [set out] in the Rasamrita-sindhu with the words "service in the form of a sadhaka," and so on.12 Here "in the form of a sadhaka" means "in the external body," and "in the form of a siddha" means "in a body conceived as suited to one's own desired service." And in that [service] in the siddha form, it is only by the path of raga; the distinctions of time, place and pastimes are manifold — how much [of them] could be written? Service in the sadhaka form, however, is to be learned by a threefold method, according to the agamas and so on. The revered Acharya Mahashaya there will instruct you in it, for he is indeed our all. What more? On the fourteenth day of [the month of] Vaishakha.

33Such is one letter.
Having heard the Gosvami's merciful letter,
all joyfully sing the Gosvami's virtues.

34Sri Govinda Kaviraja, taking leave,
went from Kheturi to the village of Budhari.

35Sitting in solitude, with a very joyful mind,
he gathers together the jewels of his songs.

36At that time a letter came from Vraja; Govinda, placing the letter on his head, reads it. The holy letter (4). Glory to Sri Vrindavana-chandra! Blessings! To the great bhagavata Sri Govinda Kaviraja, the supreme object of love, — Jiva's remembrance of Krishna. Through the good wishes of your honour, [all is] well here; [the well-being] there I ardently desire. There it is you who shine as our friend; therefore we always long to hear of your well-being — attend to this. Your songs full of descriptions of Krishna, sent now, and those [sent] earlier, satisfy us as if they were nectar; and yet, hoping for new ones, again and again we remain unsated, — so kindly attend to this as well. Further: earlier the Brihad-bhagavatamrita was sent for Sri Srinivasa Acharya Gosvami with Shyamadasa the mridanga player; write whether it has reached there or not, and free us from doubt. What more? This is written to your honour, merciful by your very nature. On the third day of the bright fortnight of [the month of] Chaitra. Here — blessings to Sriman Narottama and to Kaviraja, and this is [my] message. Here — the obeisances of Sri Krishnadasa.

37In the letter "Kaviraja" is Ramachandra;
Narottama and Ramachandra — the two are one.

38In the letter are the obeisances of Sri Krishnadasa:
this is Krishnadasa, known as Kaviraja Gosvami.

39Such is one letter.
Having read the letter, Sri Govinda, overwhelmed [with feeling],
informing his elder [brother], sent the Gitamrita.13

40What Govinda's poetry is like — what can it be compared to?
Who does not praise his virtues, who does not sing [of them]?

41Thus [it is said] in a song:
Glory to Govinda, renowned on earth,
skilled in distributing the treasure — the jewel of prema,
the Kaviraja of incomparable, sweet character! (Refrain.)

42Supremely wonderful is the arrangement of [his] poetry —
what shall I compose? [His] art is beyond fathoming.
Like a sharp arrow it pierces the heart and the head;
the rasikas reel [with delight], listening with fervour.

43There the king of the assembly of Vrinda-vipina,
Srimad Jiva, the life of the people of the world,
with a joyful heart, praising [the songs] to one another,
ever drinks the nectar-rasa of these songs.

44Srila Narottama together with Ramachandra —
their hearts overflow, the happiness cannot be told.
All the people sing, utterly maddened;
Narahari, of wicked mind, has turned away from it.14

45Hearing all this news, Acharya Thakura
cannot contain within his body the abundant bliss.

46Drawn by the Acharya, from Kheturi
Ramachandra came to Sri Yajigrama.

47Sri Acharya, seeing Ramachandra Kaviraja —
I do not know what bliss surges in [his] heart!

48When Ramachandra, prostrating himself, fell at [his] feet,
the Acharya, taking him in his embrace, bathes [him] with the tears of his eyes.

49Asking for news of Sri Narottama,
he ordered, "Go now into the house."

50Sri Ramachandra was filled with great bliss;
going [in], he bowed at the feet of the two Ishvaris.

51Draupadi Ishvari and Sri Gauranga-priya — both of them —
the motherly tenderness they showed — what can compare with it?

52Seeing Ramachandra, everyone rejoiced;
he met with all as was fitting.

53Sri Ramachandra's conduct is very sweet;
Acharya Thakura is always conquered by his love.

54What love Sri Acharya Srinivasa showed
with Ramachandra — what do I know, that I could tell it?

55Sri Ramachandra's life is most wonderful;
others have told of his virtues — [they] are known everywhere.

56Here too I had earlier thought to describe something,
[but] for fear of the length of the book I could not describe it.

57One day, on the night of the full moon, at moonrise,
Ramachandra laughs, his heart full of great joy.

58Seeing Ramachandra laughing, Draupadi Ishvari
carefully, very softly, says to Sri Acharya:

59"Why he is laughing, I cannot understand at all."
The Acharya replies, "I will tell you — listen attentively.

60Sri Radhika and Krishna, both, in a grove of flowers
are gathering flowers, surrounded by the sakhis.

61Rai picks wondrously blossoming kumuda flowers,
while Madhai by mistake picks the moonlight, [taking it] for them.

62Seeing Krishna's mistake, the sakhis laugh.
Ramachandra, being there beside me, laughs."15

63Hearing [this], Sri Ishvari was amazed at heart.
Such playful wonders he displays — what more can be said?

64With Ramachandra, Sri Acharya constantly —
his heart is overwhelmed by savouring the Gosvamis' books.

65Ramachandra Kaviraja is a man of great learning;
there is nothing to which his learning can be compared.

66In Yajigrama great bliss grows day by day;
all are utterly overwhelmed in Prabhu's sankirtana.16

67A few days later the Acharya, taking his dear [disciples],
went to the village of Kanchanagariya.

68There he became immersed in the bliss of great sankirtana
and effortlessly removed the sins of the living beings.

69Staying a few days with everyone in great happiness,
he came with the greatest delight to the village of Budhari.

70He quickly sent a man to the village of Sri Kheturi;
he reported this news to Mahashaya.

71Sri Thakura Mahashaya, with his companions,
came to the village of Budhari, his mind full of great bliss.

72What absorption in prema [there was] at their meeting —
the fortunate people beheld it to their eyes' content.

73Everyone's heart is overwhelmed by the Acharya's beauty;
who indeed does not sing of [his] enchanting beauty and virtues?

74As [it is said] in a song (raga Saranga):
Glory, glory to Srinivasa, the jewel of virtues!
Blessed, blessed is the good fortune of the earth — what a wonder:
a form full of love for Gaura has appeared! (Refrain.)

75The lustre of [his] body surpasses kunkuma, gold and the lotus;
lovely is his moon-face, his lips are nectar.
Sweet is his smile, his speech soft and charming —
as if a new, boundless nectar were raining down.

76Sandal tilaka on his forehead, brows beyond compare,
the large lotuses of his eyes brimming [with feeling].
His tender arms reach down to his knees,
his neck is like a conch, his chest adorned with a garland.17

77Beautiful is the cloth he wears, slender is his waist,
lovely the three folds [of his belly], charming the navel;
his thighs and knees delight the people.
Ghanashyama Dasa offers himself for the nails of [his] feet.18

78Again, raga Velavali:
Glory to Srinivasa Acharya, the life of the people of the world,
the supreme rasika, the abode of virtues,
the giver of refuge to the wretched, the helpless and the fallen,
the friend of the lowly, the ornament of noble deeds!

79He is exceedingly adorned with the graceful ornaments of bhava;
his body is like the champaka and the crimson flower;
the incomparable dear associate of Gaurachandra,
on seeing whom the heart cannot keep its composure.

80Renowned in the world, a cloud raining the rasa of prema,
one to whom the joy-giving master Narottama is like life itself.
Ceaselessly drinking the nectar of the Divine Couple's pastimes,
he delights, intoxicated — what more can a poet compose?

81Ah, ah! He whose servant at the feet [became]
the merciful Ramachandra Kaviraja!
What shall I say? What a new wish-fulfilling tree of bhakti this is —
for Narahari's sake [he] planted [it] in the midst of the earth.

82The beauty of Sri Narottama enraptures everyone;
who does not sing of Narottama's form and qualities?

83Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Velavali):
Glory to Sri Narottama, supreme in magnanimity!
He delights the people of the world; his luster is like a golden lotus;
as if he ceaselessly rains down flower-honey. (Refrain.)

84He glitters, adorned with abundant waves of goosebumps;
on his incomparable face, a constant gentle smile.
His trembling eyes are tinged with the rasa of compassion;
the charm of his words steals the hearing and the mind.

85An incomparable tilaka, a forehead most sweet,
his neck shining with many garlands of tulasi.
Rounded arms, lovely hands like young shoots,
a broad chest — any comparison for it falls short.

86A slender waist, new blue cloth,
full, excellent thighs of beautiful shape;
the pair of tender feet, cool, so cool,
shines in the heart of Narahari.

87The assembly of Vaishnavas, full of beauty, was captivating;
everyone saw their radiance, like that of the sun.

88The Acharya, together with all of them in the village of Budhari,
was absorbed in sankirtana day and night.

89After spending some days in bliss in the village of Sri Budhari,
he joyfully set out for the village of Borakuli.19

90Sri Govinda Chakravarti, overwhelmed with prema,
received the Acharya and his associates in his own home.20

91Chakravarti is the Acharya's dearest disciple,
expert in singing, in playing instruments and in the science [of music] — bhakti embodied.

92How Sri Govinda became the Acharya's disciple,
how he came from Mahala to Borakuli,21

93how he settled in the village of Borakuli —
what shall I describe of this? It is known everywhere.

94Joy overflowed in Sri Govinda's house:
the Acharya arrived [there] with everyone.

95He had preparations made for a great festival [mahotsava]
and sent letters of invitation everywhere.

96Virachandra came with his associates;
Krishna Mishra came, surrounded by his associates.

97Sri Gopiramana, the disciple of Sri Hridayananda,
set out from Ambika.22

98Thakura Ramai, his heart full of great jubilation,
came after taking leave before Balarama.23

99Thakura Kanai, the son of Raghunandana,
set forth from Khanda with his associates.24

100Sri Yadunandana, from Kantaka-nagara,
after bowing to Gaurachandra, set out.25

101Sri Nayanananda Mishra, in great joy,
set out, taking his dear associates with him.26

102They all came near the village of Borakuli;
who knows how to describe the joy that there was?

103Sri Acharya Thakura, Thakura Mahashaya,
Ramachandra, Shridasa, Gokulananda and others

104went out to meet them and brought everyone in;
wondrous merriment began in Govinda's house.

105That day they spent in the bliss of dancing and singing;
in the morning all performed their bath and other rites.

106All came and sat in the temple courtyard;
an unprecedented beauty arose, and everyone beheld it.

107Srinivasa Acharya had the Sri Deity brought;
seeing [Him], everyone's great joy increased.

108To perform the abhisheka and other rites
everyone gave permission to Acharya Thakura.

109Taking everyone's permission, the Acharya
joyfully performs the abhisheka and other rites.

110As they were deliberating what the Sri Deity's name should be,
suddenly a voice sounded within the temple:

111"Perform the abhisheka under the name Sri Radha-vinoda."
Hearing this, great delight of heart arose in everyone.

112Sri Acharya carefully completed all the rites,
seated [the Deity] on the throne and dressed [Him] in wondrous attire.

113The beauty of Sri Radha-vinoda is exceedingly wondrous;
seeing [Him], streams of tears flow from everyone's eyes.

114Fixing their eyes on Sri Radhika, everyone
says to one another, "What a wondrous sight!"

115Seeing both Sri Radhika and Sri Radha-vinoda,
no one can turn away their unblinking eyes.

116Countless people come — there is no counting them;
there is no limit to the joy in Govinda's house.

117Govinda's house became full of auspiciousness;
on all sides everyone raised cries of "Glory!"

118The festival of that day I am unable to tell;
but what [happened] on the next day — of that I will relate a little.

119Prabhu Virachandra, Krishna Mishra and all the others —
all performed their bath and other rites early in the morning.

120All came into the courtyard of Sri Radha-vinoda
and, floating in happiness, had darshana of Radha-vinoda.

121Shyamadasa, Devi, Gokula and others — all came
and, well prepared, began the sankirtana.27

122Shyamadasa and Devidasa play the mridanga;
how many waves of rasa arise from it!

123The soft sound of the mridanga pierces the sky;
no one can stay still on hearing the syllables of the tala.

124Gokula and the others perform the alapa of ragas in various styles;
in the raga-alapa they display intense gamakas.

125The seven svaras, the gramas and the rest became embodied;
first of all they sing the qualities of Gaurachandra.

126By the mantra of song they drew Prabhu Gaurachandra;
the Lord with His associates was as if directly present.

127Sri Narottama's voice is captivating —
as if it ceaselessly rains new nectar.

128What can compare with this sankirtana, rare even for the gods?
Everyone became supremely overwhelmed.

129Leaning his body against the body of the Acharya, who was full of prema,
Prabhu Virachandra dances, having lost his composure.

130Prabhu Krishna Mishra, the son of Advaita Acharya,
is thoroughly drenched with his own tears.

131Thakura Kanai, the son of Sri Raghunandana —
how intoxicated he is in the rapture of prema, it is impossible to say.

132Sri Nayanananda Mishra, grey with dust,
whirls about dancing — what captivating movements!

133Thakura Ramai dances with wondrous movements;
with roars and cries of "hunkara" he turns in all four directions.

134Sri Yadunandana, the disciple of Dasa Gadadhara —
who, seeing his state, would not weep?

135Sri Gopiramana Chakravarti, in the fullness of prema,
sank into the ocean of the happiness of sankirtana.

136Ramachandra, Shridasa and all the Vaishnavas
cannot keep their composure, overwhelmed by prema.

137Prabhu Virachandra, becoming still in the rapture of the dance,
weeps, embracing Narottama.

138Everyone came into supreme rapture of prema;
who embraces whom — there is no counting it.

139Forgetting themselves, all roll on the ground;
some, weeping, clasp someone's feet.

140That rapture of bhava — who can describe it?
Seeing [it], the gods consider themselves fortunate.

141When the sankirtana subsided, everyone grew calm
and, in great joy, sat in the courtyard of the Lord.28

142How everyone was absorbed in talks of the deeds of Radha-Krishna and Chaitanya —
[only] the fortunate see that.

143Growing calm, everyone praises this holy courtyard:
this courtyard is truly an ocean of prema.

144Seeing Govinda Chakravarti's rapture of bhava,
everyone was filled with boundless jubilation.

145He became renowned as "Bhavuka Chakravarti";29
who would not praise [him], seeing the manner of his prema-bhakti?

146For some days everyone in the village of Borakuli
remained, greatly enraptured in sankirtana.

147Prabhu Virachandra, Krishna Mishra and all the others
became very distressed when the time came to take leave.

148How everyone took leave and departed —
this cannot at all be described with one mouth.

149The Acharya and Thakura Mahashaya with their associates
follow behind them, tears streaming from their eyes.

150Various provisions, [gathered] with great care,
they afterwards sent [after the guests] through people.

151With Narottama and the others dear to Sri Acharya,
[he] remained for some days in Sri Borakuli.

152To which other disciples' homes he went —
that I have not described, for fear of making the book too long.

153The joy that arose in the region of Borakuli,
how bhakti increased — that I could not describe.

154By the merciful glance of Sri Acharya Thakura
all the people became deeply absorbed in sankirtana.

155In Sri Govinda's house the Acharya with his associates
beholds the beauty of Sri Radha-vinoda with great delight.

156Having made known to Sri Radha-vinoda the inner feelings [of his] heart,
[the Acharya] set out for Kheturi, crossing the Padmavati.

157Going together with everyone to Gaurachandra's courtyard,
he was overwhelmed at the darshana of the Lords.

158For some days [all] were immersed in the rasa of sankirtana
and gave great bliss to the people living in Kheturi.

159Having said something in private to Narottama, dearer to him than life,
he took his leave and came to the village of Budhari.

160Many people from other lands, seeing the Acharya,
spoke to one another of the Acharya's virtues.

161Someone said, "The Acharya is Gaura's prema embodied;
through the Acharya the Lord accomplishes many works.

162Having spread the books of the Gosvamis,
he crushed the pride of those opposed to bhakti."

163Someone said, "O brother, those turned away [from the Lord],
having become self-willed, transgress dharma.

164The one who is chief among those turned away —
they dress him up as 'Raghunatha' and deceive people.30

165That sinful villain, having composed his own doctrine,
preaches [it] in Vanga — [he is called], they say, 'Kavindra.'"31

166Someone said, "I have seen great sinners
who, abandoning the kirtana of Sri Krishna, have themselves sung of."

167Someone said, "In the land of Rarh there is a certain basest of brahmanas,
known as 'Mallik'; there is no villain equal to him.

168That sinner has himself called 'Gopala';
displaying a rakshasa's maya, he deceives people."

169Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata:32
"By that good fortune, even today the land of Vanga is blessed:
men and women perform the sankirtana of Sri Chaitanya.

170Only here and there a few sinners go about
and ruin people, hiding their [true nature].

171To fill their bellies, some of the sinners
call themselves 'Raghunatha.'

172Some sinner, abandoning all the sankirtana of Krishna,
has some ghosts sing of him himself.

173One whom I see in three conditions in a day —
how is that wretch not ashamed to have himself sung of?33

174In Rarh there is one more great brahma-daitya:34
within he is a rakshasa, a brahmana only in his dress.

175That sinner has himself called 'Gopala';
therefore everyone calls him 'Shiyala.'"35

176Someone said, "Great misfortune [awaits] them all:
the punisher of all these mlecchas is the Kalki-avatara."

177Saying this and much else with joyful hearts,
they all bowed at the feet of Srinivasa Acharya.

178The Acharya fulfilled the desires of them all
and together with everyone came to his own home in Yajigrama.

179In Yajigrama he hears from people's mouths
that Prabhu Virachandra had established dharma:

180in the land of Rarh there is a village named Kadara;
there is the home of Sri Mangala [and] Jnanadasa.36

181There lived the kayastha Jayagopala;
from pride of learning an evil disposition arose in him.

182[His] guru was without learning — this [he] thought utterly contemptible;
when asked, he named his parama-guru as his guru.37

183Prabhu Virachandra by some means brought [this] to light:
[the man] had slighted [his] grace — therefore [Virachandra] cast him off.38

184Hearing this, the Acharya rejoiced at heart;
at that time a message arrived from Virachandra.

185With the greatest respect the Acharya took the letter
and reads the message, his heart blossoming with joy.

185aVictory to Sri Gaura and Nityananda!39
Your Sri Virachandra-deva, ever to be remembered [by you], with an embrace of love submits:40
"O Srila Srinivasa Acharya! You are the shakti of Sri Sri Mahaprabhu.
Therefore by one shakti the books were revealed through Srimad Rupa Gosvami and others, forms of the Lord's shakti;
by the other shakti you spread the books in Gauda-mandala, in the assembly of mahajanas.
Therefore I send you my message.
Jayagopala Dasa has slighted my grace, and this is known in the world;
therefore here none of my people holds conversation and so on with him —
I too have forbidden it — and you too should not hold conversation and so on with him."

186Having sent such a letter from Kadara,
Prabhu went to Khardaha and told [of it] to his sons.41

187Just as Prabhu Virachandra is an abode of virtues,
so his three sons are full of prema-bhakti.

188The eldest son is known as "Gopijana-vallabha,"42
the middle one is Sri Ramakrishna, supremely generous,

189the youngest is Sri Ramachandra, supremely gentle;
some fortunate one will describe the lives of these three.

190Who does not weep [with love, hearing] of Prabhu Virachandra's virtues?
He cast off the sinful Jayagopala.

191All these matters became known everywhere;
no one ever [again] held conversation and so on [with him].

192In Yajigrama the Acharya with his disciples
always spends [his time] in discussion of the shastras and in sankirtana.

193The names of the disciples I could not write here:
I have set [them] out in detail in the book Srinivasa-charitra.43

194Whose heart is not soothed by the Acharya's virtues?
Who does not sing of the Acharya's life?

195In a song — raga Kamoda:
He is my life and soul, the supremely merciful Acharya Thakura Srinivasa;
his body surpassing gold, known throughout the world — the manifestation of Sri Chaitanya's prema.

196All who are dear to Chaitanya constantly show him tenderness; how could I tell of his virtues? From an early age, his mind skilled in learning, he always meditated on Chaitanya's feet.

197One day, at the end of the night, Sri Chaitanya, moved by tenderness, taking Nitaichand with Him, came to Srinivasa and, in the guise of a dream, laughing and laughing, speaks, looking at Srinivasa's face:

198"Go quickly to Vrindavana: there Rupa and Sanatana have composed wonderful books. I shall distribute [them] through you." Saying this again and again, [He] entrusted [him] to Nityananda.

199Then the dream broke; unable to control his body, Srinivasa was overwhelmed. Wandering in that rapture of prema through Nilachala and the land of Gauda, he set out for Vrindavana.

200With many longings in his heart, rejoicing, within a few days he entered the city of Mathura. Hearing there of the departure of both — Sri Rupa and Sanatana — he fell senseless.

201Regaining consciousness he weeps and, rolling on the ground, says, "Ha, ha, Prabhu Rupa-Sanatana! Why have you deprived [me]? I do not understand this play! Why have [you] kept [me] alive?"

202Knowing his heart to be so grieved, Rupa and Sanatana came in the guise of a dream, in a rapture of prema; taking Srinivasa on their laps, wiping away [his] tears, they speak in the sweetest words:

203"Go quickly to Vrindavana and surrender yourself at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta. Think of no sorrow — you will attain the highest happiness; thus the two of us will appear to you."

204Having said this, Rupa and Sanatana vanished; Srinivasa, rising at dawn,
enters Vrindavana — streams of prema from both eyes — beholding the beauty of Vrindavana.

205Sri Jiva, obtaining Srinivasa, in a rapture of bliss brought [him] to meet the Gosvamis. By Sri Rupa's command in a dream, Sri Gopala Bhatta with great tenderness made Srinivasa his disciple.

206How much tenderness Sri Jiva Gosani [had] — who can tell? He made [him] learned in the shastras. Within a few days Srinivasa, joyful at heart, met his dear Narottama.

207Taking Narottama with him, he joyfully wandered through Vraja; obtaining Govinda's garland of command,44 [they] distributed the books of the Gosvamis, settling in Sri Gauda-mandala.

208Drinking the nectar of Gaura's prema, he is ever intoxicated with sankirtana; his fame resounds in the world. Lowly Narahari says: he delivers by his own goodness — there is no one else so merciful.

209Again, raga Velavali:
Glory, glory to Sri Srinivasa, the abode of virtues!
Deliverer of the poor and wretched, elixir of prema — such is [his] sweet name. (Refrain.)

210His body, stealing [the lustre] of the colour of gold, is lovely; silk garments shine upon it. Calling [it] prema, the bhagavatas say: with that very colour [his] body is adorned.45

211Together with his own devotees and associates he revealed his beautiful lotus feet.
Ceaselessly on [his] lips shines the name: "Radhe Krishna Govinde."

212Worship of the Divine Couple, relishing of the lilas, in his hand the wish-fulfilling tree of books. Apart from you, who will give shelter to the fallen, helpless Govindadasa?46

213I could not describe the Acharya's life even in part;
somehow or other I have only brought about my own good fortune.

214Sri Thakura Mahashaya is dear to the Acharya;
who does not sing of his life, full of prema?

215In a song — raga Kamoda:
O my merciful Sri Thakura Mahashaya, Narottama — prema embodied!
How tender is his body, like a shirisha flower; the radiance of his body surpasses gold.

216In his youth nothing pleased him; hearing of Gora's virtues, he always wept.
Renouncing royal enjoyments, quite unnoticed, he went to Vrajapura.

217Entering Vrindavana, his heart full of supreme bliss, he surrendered himself to Lokanatha. In his mercy Lokanatha accepted him as his own and gave [him] initiation into the mantra of Radha-Krishna.

218Seeing Narottama's conduct, all in Vrindavana were happy and loved him as their own life. What intimate [bond he had] with Srinivasa Acharya — who knows it? One soul, only the bodies different.

219Seeing Sri Radha-vinoda, he always delights his eyes, devoted to the service of Prabhu Lokanatha.47 In studying the scriptures of bhakti great bliss grows in his heart; all [his] desires were fulfilled.

220With Prabhu's permission he went from Sri Vraja-mandala into Sri Gauda-mandala. By the strength of Prabhu's grace he wandered through the homes of devotees in Navadvipa and Nilachala.

221How sweet [his] way of life — his dwelling in the village of Kheturi: he serves Gaura, Sri Radha-ramana, [the Deity] named Sri Vallavikanta, Radha-kanta, the abode of rasa, Radha-Krishna, Sri Vrajamohana.48

222These six Deities seem to sport there in person; who, seeing [Their] beauty, would not forget [all else]? With dear Ramachandra, Narottama, in great delight, floats on the waves of the rasa of prema.49

223However many Narottama's virtues — who can tell how many? In his sankirtana there is a rain of prema. Sri Advaita, Nityananda, Gaurachandra with [His] associates dance — [this] the fortunate have seen.

224Narottama, great-minded, very dear to Gaura's associates, is renowned for his service to the Vaishnavas. How wondrously merciful he is: to whom does he not give the pure chintamani of bhakti?

225Pashandas and asuras he intoxicated with Gora's virtues, himself beside himself in the rapture of prema. Whose deeds are beyond this world — will there ever be another such? His is the fame proclaimed from land to land.

226Lowly Narahari says: will there be such a day, [when] I shall be sold at Narottama's feet? Ceaselessly raising both arms, crying "Prabhu Narottama!", shall I roll weeping in the dust?

227Again, raga Deshapala (the rangavardhini metre):50 Glory to Narottama Mahashaya, adorned with auspiciousness, the excellent pandita — charming is all his way — most honoured, deep, utterly steadfast, the abode of virtues! His form, full of prema, a well of rasa, beyond compare; intoxicated, day and night he is devoted to singing new melodies; his gait and dance captivate the heart, his tender body is beautiful.

228Ceaselessly serving the beautiful Deities, he is in great joy; the beloved of Gaurahari's devotees, renowned for compassion; friend of the wretched, who fulfilled all [their] desires. His most charming fame is the ornament of the world, without blemish; no end is found to [his] boundless virtues; the hosts of great poets sing [them] ceaselessly — [and so does] the servant Ghanashyama.51

229The beautiful deeds of Sri Narottama are boundless;
how can I, worthless, describe them with one mouth?

230Who does not weep [with love, hearing] of the virtues of Sri Thakura Mahashaya?
When one meditates on [his] life, all inauspiciousness goes far away.

231Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the Bhakti-ratnakara.

Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the fourteenth wave, called "The Description of Srimad Acharya's Travels to the Homes of His Disciples, and Other Events".

Notes

  1. Acharyaratna is the title of Chandrashekhara Acharya, a relative and associate of the Lord (CC Adi 10).
  2. Jiva Gosvami's four letters (18, 22, 32, 36) are written in Sanskrit prose; in the 1960 edition they stand outside the numbering of the couplets. Sri Vrindavana-natha ("the Lord of Vrindavana") and Sri Vrindavana-chandra ("the Moon of Vrindavana," 32, 36) are Krishna.
  3. The titles by the scan of A: শ্রীরসামৃতসিন্ধু-শ্রীমাধবমহোৎসবোত্তরচম্পূ-হরিনামামৃতানাং (rasāmṛtasindhu … harināmāmṛtānām). The Madhava-mahotsava is Jiva's poem on the coronation of Radha as queen of Vrindavana; the Uttara-champu is the second part of the Gopala-champu (cf. 22).
  4. "[Convey]": A (scan) reads বাচ্যাঃ (vācyāḥ, "are to be told").
  5. Bhadra is the month of August–September; sudi is the bright (waxing) half of the month. No day is given (A, scan: ইতি ভাদ্র সুদী).
  6. Srinivasa's son, named by Jiva Gosvami (20); not to be confused with Vrindavana Dasa Thakura, the author of CB.
  7. By the scan of A: বিরোধী ভগবদ্ভক্তের্বিদাহীন্দ্রিয়দেহয়োঃ শোকস্তথাপি কর্ত্তব্যো যদি শোচো নিবর্ত্ততে (virodhī bhagavad-bhakter vidāhīndriya-dehayoḥ / śokas tathāpi kartavyo yadi śoco nivartate); śoco is taken as śocyo, "the one mourned": grief would be fitting only if it brought him back. The opening of the letter in A: স্বস্তি মুখমিদং— শমিহ সমীহিতং শ্রীবৃন্দাবনবাসরূপং বসত্যেব (svasti-mukham idaṃ: śam iha, samīhitaṃ śrī-vṛndāvana-vāsa-rūpaṃ vasaty eva).
  8. The Vaishnava-toshani is a commentary on the Tenth Canto of the Bhagavatam; the Durgama-sangamani is Jiva's commentary on the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu; the Hari-namamrita-vyakarana is Jiva's Sanskrit grammar, in which the rules are set out through the names of Krishna (bhashya and vritti are kinds of commentary); the Uttara-gopala-champu is the second part of the Gopala-champu.
  9. In A (scan) the cluster is printed indistinctly (শ্র…ত্বানুধ্যানং), in the 1960 ed. by OCR śaratvāmudhyānaṃ; understood as śaśvad-anudhyānaṃ, "constant remembrance."
  10. The 1912/13 ed. notes a variant reading: vidyāvān, "learned," instead of vidyamāna, "now living." Vyasa Acharya is Vyasa Chakravarti, a disciple of Srinivasa (21).
  11. The 1912/13 ed. notes that one manuscript has "Srinivasa" in place of "Sri Govinda."
  12. Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2.295: "Service [is to be rendered] in the form of a sadhaka and in the form of a siddha…". The agamas are scriptures on temple worship and ritual.
  13. The Gitamrita is the collection of songs of Govinda Dasa Kaviraja; his elder brother is Ramachandra Kaviraja.
  14. Narahari is the poet's signature.
  15. The kumuda is the white water lily that opens in the moonlight. Srinivasa and Ramachandra, in their spiritual (siddha) forms, are present at the pastime of Radha and Krishna (cf. Jiva's letter in 14.32).
  16. Prabhu here is apparently Srinivasa Acharya.
  17. "Chest" — the 1912/13 and 1960 eds. have uru ("thigh"), understood as ura ("chest").
  18. "Offers himself" is nichhani (nichhani). Ghanashyama Dasa is the poet's signature (the second name of Narahari Chakravarti).
  19. Borakuli is the village where Govinda Chakravarti, a disciple of Srinivasa, lived (see 90–93); here Srinivasa installed his Deity, Sri Radha-vinoda (110–111). The 1960 edition's section heading before 89 is omitted.
  20. Govinda Chakravarti, a disciple of Srinivasa and a skilled singer, was called "Bhavuka Chakravarti" for his ecstasies (145). "Received" follows A: the scan reads গণসহ আচার্য্যে দিলেন নিজালয়ে (dilen, lit. "gave [shelter] in his own home"); the 1960 edition has milen ("met").
  21. Mahala is the village from which Govinda Chakravarti moved to Borakuli; the author gives no further details.
  22. Gopiramana (in 135, Gopiramana Chakravarti) was a disciple of Hridayananda (Hridaya Chaitanya) of Ambika (Kalna).
  23. Thakura Ramai is apparently Ramachandra (Ramai), the adopted son and disciple of Jahnava Ishvari; Balarama here is probably the Deity of Balarama whom he served. The identification is tentative.
  24. Thakura Kanai is the son of Raghunandana of Shrikhanda; Khanda is Shrikhanda.
  25. Yadunandana was a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa (see 134); Gaurachandra is the Deity of Mahaprabhu at Kantaka-nagara (Katwa).
  26. Nayanananda Mishra was a Vaishnava poet, the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita.
  27. Shyamadasa, Devi (Devidasa) and Gokula are musicians and singers of the circle of Srinivasa and Narottama; Shyamadasa and Devidasa play the mridanga (122), Gokula sings (124).
  28. The courtyard of the Lord is the courtyard of the temple of Sri Radha-vinoda (cf. 120).
  29. Bhavuka (bhāvuka) means "full of bhava, ecstatic."
  30. Raghunatha is a name of Rama: this man is passed off as an incarnation of the Lord (cf. 171).
  31. Reading unclear: কহয়ে কবীন্দ্র বঙ্গদেশেতে প্রচার (kahaye kabīndra baṅgadeśete pracāra), so in G and B, confirmed by the scan of A; "Kavindra" ("king of poets") is apparently a nickname or title of this false teacher.
  32. The quotation (169–175) is CB Adi-khanda 14 (on the Lord's journey through East Bengal); there Vrindavana Dasa speaks of the false incarnations of his own time.
  33. Dine tina avasthā, "three conditions in a day": i.e. he is subject to bodily changes like any ordinary person.
  34. A brahma-daitya is the ghost of a dead brahmana, a demon.
  35. Śiyāla means "jackal"; a mocking echo of "Gopala."
  36. Kadara (Kandra) is a village in Rarh (now in Purba Bardhaman district), the birthplace of the poet Jnanadasa. "শ্রীমঙ্গল জ্ঞানদাসের" is taken as two persons: Mangala Thakura and Jnanadasa, both of Kadara.
  37. The parama-guru is the guru of one's guru.
  38. Prasāda means "grace," and also the sanctified remnants of food; which is meant here the text does not show (cf. the letter at 185a: "has slighted my grace").
  39. Virachandra's letter (Sanskrit prose) is in A/B and in the 1960 edition, but the 1960 edition gives it no number; the number 185a follows the sequence.
  40. By the scan of A: ভবদীয়াবশ্যস্মরণীয়-শ্রীবীরচন্দ্রদেবঃ (bhavadīyāvaśya-smaraṇīya-), i.e. bhavadīya-avaśya-smaraṇīya, "yours, ever to be remembered."
  41. "To his sons": so A (scan) and the 1960 edition (পুত্রে, putre).
  42. Gopijana-vallabha, Ramakrishna and Ramachandra are the sons of Virachandra.
  43. A work by Narahari himself on the life of Srinivasa Acharya.
  44. The garland of command (ājñā-mālā) is a garland from the Deity of Govinda in Vrindavana, given as a sign of command.
  45. Reading unclear: প্রেম-নাম করি কহত ভাগবতে (prema-nāma kari kahata bhāgavate) — bhāgavate is taken as "the bhagavatas" (devotees); "in the Bhagavata" is also possible. The reading is confirmed by the scan of A.
  46. Govindadasa is the poet Govindadasa Kaviraja, a disciple of Srinivasa; this is his signature in the song.
  47. Radha-vinoda here is the Deity of Lokanatha Gosvami in Vrindavana (not the Deity in Govinda Chakravarti's house, 156).
  48. The six Deities of Kheturi (cf. BR 10.483): Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Vrajamohana, Krishna, Radha-kanta, Radha-ramana; "Radha-Krishna" here is Sri Krishna (with Radha).
  49. Ramachandra is Ramachandra Kaviraja, Narottama's closest friend.
  50. Rangavardhini is the name of a poetic metre (chhanda).
  51. Ghanashyama is the poetic name of Narahari Chakravarti.
